assertions.name: A4_three_regime_reading_is_affected
assertions.source: both A=3 isotopes move from inside to above once the ceiling is corrected for sub-additivity

description: Reconciles this session's bond measurements with the active qou-brng arc's he4_exceeds_pairwise_maximum_probe. The bond constants agree to 1.3e-13 by two independent routes — Markov-trace ratios in H_6/H_9 here, the closed form -log(z+d) there — which validates both. But that probe's B_allpairs sums the bond multiset, and all-pairs is sub-additive: a non-adjacent bond built as the braid band generator delivers only ~0.65 of its isolated value once the adjacent bonds are present (0.659916, 0.650555, 0.640829, 0.625186 measured). So B_allpairs overstates the ceiling. Against the MEASURED A=3 all-pairs traces — no extrapolation — and the sibling's own alpha = 4.18598136 MeV, 3H gives AME/allpairs = 1.00418 and 3He 1.09950, i.e. both ABOVE the ceiling, where the naive-additive version put them inside at 0.945 and 0.940. That affects the three-regime conclusion: if the correction holds, a many-body term is needed at A=3 as well as A=4. The 3H agreement at 0.42% is explicitly NOT claimed as predictive — it is one number out of three, with 3He at 9.95% and 2H at 21.48%.
caveats: TWO CONVENTIONS ARE MIXED HERE AND THAT IS NOT YET RESOLVED. alpha is the sibling probe's normalisation taken as-is, while the L values are this arc's Markov traces WITHOUT their -(e/2) log(1-h) charge term. The -log(z+d) cores agree to 1e-13, but the charge term is not cross-checked and is the one real convention difference between the two arcs. No number here is quotable as a prediction until that is reconciled; what survives the caveat is the DIRECTION of the correction, since lowering a ceiling can only move isotopes from inside it to above it.

THE SATURATION FACTOR IS MEASURED AT A = 3 ONLY, for a single far-bond configuration per nucleus. The A=3 numbers in A3 use the directly measured all-pairs traces and so do not depend on it, but any extension to A >= 4 would be extrapolating a factor from two data points. The 4He and 6Li figures are deliberately not carried here for that reason.

This CHANGES a sibling's published conclusion rather than confirming it, on a branch that arc has not seen. It is offered as a flag for qou-brng to check, not as a settled overturn — the convention mixing above is exactly the kind of thing that could account for a 5-10% shift, which is the size of the effect that moves 3H and 3He across the line.
